senses.definition: Coming across as calm, clear and senior enough to be handed a decision.
distractors: A record of delivering what you promised, quarter after quarter.
The number of people who report to you, directly and indirectly.
The ability to speak a second language well enough to negotiate in it.
The set of decisions a leader is formally allowed to make without asking.
The rank a job sits at in a company's grading system, published for everyone to see.

senses.definition: Skill in handling something delicate so smoothly that the difficulty never shows.
distractors: Brute force applied until an obstacle gives way.
Doing a job to a standard nobody asked for, at a cost nobody agreed to.
A rehearsed answer prepared in advance for a question you expect to be asked.
The willingness to say the uncomfortable thing in a room that does not want to hear it.
The care taken to record exactly how a decision was reached, so it can be audited later.
